items.headline: Anthropic makes record-breaking Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19 after pricing its IPO at $83 and raising roughly $81 billion at about a $1.5 trillion valuation, the largest IPO in history. The listing is a major test of investor appetite for AI-lab valuations amid growing bubble concerns.

items.headline: Asian markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
items.summary: Stock markets across Asia fell sharply, with the Nasdaq Composite erasing its 2026 gains, as investors grew more skeptical about the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending. The selloff underscores widening doubts on Wall Street about whether AI capital expenditure can be justified by returns.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI launched two new models, with Astra priced 20% cheaper than its predecessor and positioned for demanding professional work, while Sol targets everyday use. Astra is the first model OpenAI has deployed externally that meets the 'High' threshold for AI self-improvement under its Preparedness Framework, drawing added safety scrutiny.

items.headline: Four nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceXSI to halt frontier AI development
items.summary: A coalition including Public Citizen and the Alliance for Secure AI filed suit in San Francisco Superior Court seeking an injunction—not damages—to freeze advanced AI research at five major companies, relying on California's unfair competition law in an untested legal theory.

items.headline: Nvidia expands chip supply chain deals with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics
items.summary: Nvidia announced new long-term agreements to add substrate capacity and expand production at existing factories, part of its push to secure components for sustained AI data-center chip growth amid continued demand for its GPUs.

items.headline: Nvidia unveils HPC and AI platform advances at Supercomputing '26
items.summary: At the SC26 show in Chicago, Nvidia detailed next-generation GPU and CPU platforms, networking and interconnect technology, and systems aimed at large-scale agentic AI and scientific computing workloads, reinforcing its push to dominate AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini Robotics 2.5
items.summary: DeepMind's most capable vision-language-action model to date is rolling out to robotics partners to improve dexterity, reliability and safety in real-world robot tasks, continuing the push toward general-purpose embodied AI.

items.headline: Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid hits 96% success rate in Mercedes-Benz factory pilot
items.summary: Apollo 2 humanoid robots ran on active Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany, achieving a 96% task success rate in a proof-of-concept, a notable data point in the race to prove humanoid robots can work reliably in real factories.

items.headline: DeepMind unveils AlphaGenome 2
items.summary: Google DeepMind released an updated model for predicting how DNA sequence variants affect cell types, aimed at improving scientific understanding of disease mechanisms—part of a broader push by DeepMind into AI-driven biology research.

items.headline: Alibaba opens limited preview of Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba launched a time-limited preview of Qwen4-Max, the first public model from its Qwen4 family, featuring a 1-million-token context window. The preview runs only through November 25 and is accessible solely via a subscription plan, with no benchmarks or pricing yet disclosed.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of IPO
items.summary: Anthropic introduced two new Claude variants focused on coding and office/agentic work just before its Wall Street debut, with Fable 5.2 reportedly scoring 41.3% on the Remote Labor Index, as the company sought to showcase technical momentum to investors.
